- [USER] Requested a list of strengthening exercises for the antagonist muscles of the iliotibial band.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided a list of strengthening exercises, including:
  1. Lunges: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend one knee and lower towards the floor, keeping the back straight and chest forward. Return to starting position and repeat for the other leg.
  2. Squats: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend knees and lower towards the floor as if sitting in a chair. Return to starting position and repeat.
  3. Deadlifts: Stand with a weight in the right hand, bend knees and lean forward, keeping the back straight. Return to starting position and repeat for the other leg.
  4. Adductor exercises: Lying on one side, bend legs and lift the upper leg upwards. Hold the position for a few seconds and repeat for the other leg.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Continued the list of strengthening exercises:
  5. Abductor exercises: Lying on one side, bend legs and lift the lower leg upwards. Hold the position for a few seconds and repeat for the other leg.
  6. Step-ups: Place a step or chair in front of you, put the right foot on it and push up to lift yourself. Repeat for the other leg.
  7. Lateral lunges: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend one knee and lower towards the floor laterally, keeping the back straight and chest forward. Return to starting position and repeat for the other leg.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is important to perform these exercises correctly to avoid injury, especially if not accustomed to regular exercise. It is recommended to seek supervision from a healthcare professional, such as a physiotherapist, to ensure exercises are performed correctly and tailored to individual needs.
